claim_text: We are making positive progress in improving our safety performance and we recognise that there is still much more to do as we focus on our safety culture through leadership, robust systems, engaged behaviours and safe environments.
metric_name: Total recordable injuries; TRIFR; Total lost-time injuries
value_unit: Total recordable injuries FY25;Total recordable injuries FY24;TRIFR FY25;TRIFR FY24;Total LTI FY25;Total LTI FY24
context_text: [Table]Lag indicators FY25 FY24 FY23 Total recordable injuries 19 39 58. TRIFR 10.2 10.4 16.0. Total lost-time injuries 5 2 3.
label: Partially Supported
rationale_short: Some safety indicators improved, including total recordable injuries and TRIFR, but lost-time injuries increased from 2 to 5, so the claim is only partially supported.
llm_reason: The claim’s decisive assertion is that the company is making positive progress in improving safety performance, while also focusing on safety culture through leadership, systems, behaviours, and safe environments. The evidence substantiates some improvement in safety performance: total recordable injuries decreased from 39 (FY24) to 19 (FY25) and TRIFR decreased slightly from 10.4 (FY24) to 10.2 (FY25). However, the evidence also shows total lost-time injuries increased from 2 (FY24) to 5 (FY25), which weakens an unqualified “positive progress” framing for overall safety performance. Additionally, the evidence provides no factual support for the claimed focus on safety culture elements (leadership, robust systems, engaged behaviours, safe environments) beyond the injury-rate table.
